description: Transaction-tier verdict meta-vectors: (actual, expected, claims_cost) -> grade_transaction verdict. A comparator implementation is conformant iff it reproduces every `verdict`. Encodes the tx-tier grading from grade_transaction: independent valid + cost dimensions (cost graded on an accepted spend when the vector carries one and the runner claims the cost dimension; a claimed null is coal, as on the eval tier); panicked and not-implemented reuse the shared vocabulary. Notable: reject + errored is coal (valid=value) — BY DESIGN differs from the eval reject arm where errored IS the clean reject. The tx tier separates clean-reject (valid:false, error:null) from failed-verdict (error:errored, valid:null).

cases.name: accept-cost-unclaimed
cases.description: A runner that does not claim the cost dimension (manifest cost:false): cost is not graded, whatever it answers.

cases.name: accept-cost-null-while-claimed-is-coal
cases.description: A runner that claims the cost dimension and answers cost:null on an accepted spend is cost-not-implemented: coal on the cost dimension, as on the eval tier.

cases.name: accept-expected-cost-null-is-na
cases.description: A value-only vector (expected.cost null): cost is not graded, even for a runner that claims it.

cases.name: reject-errored-coal
cases.description: BY DESIGN: errored on a reject vector is coal, not a clean rejection. The tx tier explicitly separates clean-reject (valid:false, error:null) from failed-verdict (error:errored, valid:null). Differs from the eval reject arm where errored IS the clean reject.
